# Media pipelines with your own keys

**Price a shot list, generate images, video, voice and avatars inside caps and approvals, keep provenance, hand off to posting.**

Builds cost-controlled AI media pipelines with @useclaudia/media and claudia generate — images (Nano Banana, GPT Image, FLUX, Seedream), video (Gemini Omni, Veo 3.1, Kling, Seedance, Hailuo, Wan, Runway), speech and music (ElevenLabs, Gemini TTS, Lyria), talking avatars and lip-sync (HeyGen, OmniHuman) on the person's own provider keys, with dry-run estimates for a whole shot list, per-job/day/month caps, approvals, a restart-safe job queue, brand kits, a local library with provenance sidecars, ffmpeg post-processing and hand-off to social posting. Use when someone wants to batch-produce content, price a shoot before spending, chain image → video → voice → avatar, wire media into an agent or app, or debug over_budget, needs_approval, blocked or expired jobs.

## How it works

1. Write the brief and shot list
2. Price the whole list
3. Set caps and the approval line
4. Generate and wait
5. Keep consistency with a brand kit
6. Library, provenance and post-processing
7. Hand off to posting
8. Review spend

The full instructions are in **[SKILL.md](SKILL.md)**: when to use it, what you need, every step, the checks before you
finish, and the pitfalls.

## Install

```sh
# Claude Code (all projects on this machine)
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills
curl -fsSLo /tmp/media-pipelines.zip https://useclaudia.xyz/skills/media-pipelines.zip
unzip -oq /tmp/media-pipelines.zip -d ~/.claude/skills

# Codex and other agents that read ~/.agents/skills
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills && unzip -oq /tmp/media-pipelines.zip -d ~/.agents/skills
```

Or straight from GitHub with the [`skills` CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills):
`npx skills add claudia-onchain/Claudia-Skills --skill media-pipelines`.

In the Claude apps: **Customize → Skills → + → Upload a skill**, and pick `media-pipelines.zip` (don't unzip it).
More apps: [install a skill](../../../README.md#install-a-skill).

Then ask for the task in your own words, or call it directly with `/media-pipelines`.
